study_identification_part.si_4_title: Personalizing progressive changes to brain structure in Alzheimer's disease using normative modeling

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used a non-Gaussian Bayesian regression model (warped Bayesian linear regression) that accounts for non-Gaussian distributions of neuroimaging data and adjusts for site effects. The model was trained on 58,836 scans from 82 sites to generate normative models per region.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: A non-Gaussian Bayesian regression model was implemented, which accounts for the non-Gaussian distributions of the cortical thickness and subcortical volume data and adjusts for unwanted noise from scanning acquisition across multiple sites.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Verdi2024.pdf.md: Section 2.4 Neuroanatomical normative modeling / Line 145

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Cortical thickness of 148 cortical regions and gray matter tissue volume of 20 subcortical volumes from the Destrieux parcellations were extracted using FreeSurfer recon-all.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: T1-weighted scans from both the reference and the research dataset were processed using FreeSurfer recon-all cross-sectional, to extract the cortical thickness of 148 cortical regions and gray matter tissue volume of 20 subcortical volumes from the Destrieux parcellations.
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Verdi2024.pdf.md: Section 2.3 Estimation of cortical thickness and subcortical volumes / Line 141

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative models were generated using age, sex, and site as covariates. The model was trained on the reference dataset and then calibrated to ADNI using transfer learning to reduce site and software version effects.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: This model was trained on 58,836 scans from datasets across 82 sites to generate normative models per region using the covariates age, sex, and site, as previously described.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.location: Verdi2024.pdf.md: Section 2.4 Neuroanatomical normative modeling / Line 145
